title: The Grihya Sutras, Part II: Gobhila, Hiraṇyakeśin and Âpastamba
altTitles: Sacred Books of the East, vol. 30
attributionNote: The sutras are ascribed to Gobhila, Hiranyakesin and Apastamba and belong to the Sama and Yajur Vedic schools. They are cumulative school texts, not the work of one author.
description: The second volume of the Grihya Sutras carries the domestic ritual of the Sama and Yajur schools: Gobhila's manual of the Sama Veda, Hiranyakesin's and Apastamba's sutras of the Black Yajurveda, and the short Yajnaparibhasha-sutras on the order of the sacrifice. Marriage, the daily and seasonal offerings, the rites of the ancestors and the expiations for ritual error are set out in their school variants, so the volume shows how far practice differed between Vedic traditions.
historicalContext: Oldenberg completed his translation of the domestic ritual in 1892 as SBE 30, adding the Sama Vedic Gobhila and the Yajurvedic Hiranyakesin and Apastamba to the Rigvedic texts of SBE 29. The volume remains the standard English rendering of these sutras.
availabilityNote: Complete. Gobhila, Hiranyakesin and Apastamba's grihya sutras with the Yajnaparibhasha-sutras are streamed from the Internet Sacred Text Archive at read time, one printed section per chapter. The volume's title page, contents, introduction and index are not part of the work.
